guides.title: Belisarius Guide
guides.summary: Dominate the open field with lightning speed and master the art of farmer hunting! 🐎 The complete strategy guide for the epic Cavalry commander, Belisarius.  Discover why Belisarius is a premier budget pick for early-game skirmishing and KvK 1, thanks to his unmatched mobility, high march speed buffs, and target debuffs. Learn how to maximize his Mobility talent tree build to hunt gatherers and weaker marches with hit-and-run tactics, pair him with speed demons like Cao Cao and Baibars, and avoid defensive traps where his frail stats can get punished!
guides.content_markdown:
Belisarius Guide

Made by: Peanut (benjamin.rok)

Should you invest in Belisarius?

● Strong in the early stages, especially for hunting and KvK1 — invest into his Mobility tree.

● Belisarius can be genuinely powerful in the earlier stages of the game, including KvK1, if you invest into his Mobility talent tree.

● His mobility lets you run around efficiently hunting down farmers and weaker targets.

● He also performs well in Sunset Canyon, giving him solid multi-mode value for an epic commander.

What makes Belisarius strong?

● His active skill deals direct damage while boosting his own march speed, letting him chase down targets effectively.

● As a Cavalry commander with Peacekeeping:Mobility specialty, he's built specifically for fast open field skirmishing.

● He can apply useful debuffs to targets, adding to his effectiveness in extended chases.

Best Talent Trees:

- Open Field:

 

Best Pairings:

1. Cao Cao

Both mobility-focused cavalry commanders combine for an extremely fast, efficient farmer-hunting march.

- Baibars

Baibars's speed and debuffs pair naturally with Belisarius's own mobility kit for open field dominance.

Tips and Tricks:

● Invest into his Mobility tree specifically — that's where his real strength lies.

● Use him to hunt down gatherers and weaker players efficiently in the early-to-mid game.

● Take advantage of his Sunset Canyon performance as an additional use case.

Biggest Mistakes:

● Do not build him without prioritizing the Mobility tree — other builds waste his core strength.

● Do not expect him to hold up as a primary commander deep into the late game.

● Do not use him for garrison or defense, which aren't part of his kit's focus.

guides.title: Boudica Guide
guides.summary: Power up your early-game account with the ultimate Peacekeeping engine! 🪓 The definitive tactical breakdown for the versatile epic commander, Boudica.  Discover why Boudica is a essential starter investment for new accounts, acting as the premier early-game barbarian-smashing machine and commander leveller. Learn how her direct damage and universal Integration kit provide broad flexibility, build her optimal Peacekeeping talent tree, and explore early-game pairings with Sun Tzu and Joan of Arc to power up your PVE progression while avoiding open-field traps!
guides.content_markdown:
Boudica Guide

Made by: Peanut (benjamin.rok)

Should you invest in Boudica?

● Great for newer players farming barbarians, but fragile in real fights.

● Boudica is an extremely effective barbarian-smashing commander, making her a great pick for newer players trying to level up their roster.

● She combines well with almost any other epic commander, giving her broad flexibility as a secondary.

● Her big downside is that she offers no defensive utility, which can make your march fragile in real PvP fights.

What makes Boudica strong?

● Her active skill deals solid direct damage, efficient against barbarians and weaker PvE targets.

● As an Integration commander, she isn't tied to a specific troop type, adding flexibility to your army composition.

● She's an accessible, easy-to-unlock epic commander for newer accounts.

Best Talent Trees:

- Peacekeeping:

 

Best Pairings:

1. Sun Tzu

Sun Tzu's defensive buffs cover Boudica's lack of survivability, forming a well-rounded epic pairing.

- Joan of Arc

Joan's rage support speeds up Boudica's skill cycling, making barbarian farming even faster.

Tips and Tricks:

● Use her primarily for barbarian hunting and leveling up other commanders early on.

● Pair her with a defensively-oriented commander to offset her fragility.

● Don't rely on her alone in real PvP engagements without defensive support.

Biggest Mistakes:

● Do not use her in serious PvP fights without a defensive secondary or support — she can fall quickly.

● Do not expect strong canyon performance; she's rated only average there.

● Do not over-invest in her expertise once you have stronger legendaries available for the same role.

guides.title: Epic commander tier list (kvk 1)
guides.summary: This guide, curated by RokNut Academy Peanut The RokNut, provides a comprehensive ranking and tactical breakdown of Epic Commanders in Rise of Kingdoms, further supported by expert analysis from Chisgule Gaming in the video "Epic Tier List [Best Commander Summer 2026] ROK - Rise of Kingdoms". Using the tier list found In The Guide, the guide organizes commanders from C to S+ tier, highlighting Sun Tzu and Baibars as the premier choices for KVK 1 and 2 due to their superior Area of Effect (AoE) damage. It also distinguishes between specialized roles, such as Lohar and Boudica for peacekeeping and Queen Tamar and Mathilda for farming. Additionally, the guide outlines a "Top 7" commander pairing list, recommending synergies like Sun Tzu + YSG to maximize early-game combat efficiency. For deeper mechanical insights, including talent builds and rage management, the Chisgule Gaming video offers detailed explanations on why specific commanders like Hermann and Imhotep are highly effective in competitive scenarios.
guides.content_markdown:
Epic commander tier list

Made by benjamin.rok (Peanut)

Individual tier list:

Farmers: 

- Queen Tamar of Georgia: not usable for fights. Good for farming.  

- Mathilda of Flanders: not usable for fights. Good for farming. Actually very good in sunset canyon!  

- Joan of Arc: is usable for fighting because of her healing factor. But it is not as good as it was once.

Peacekeeping: 

- Keira: not the best option for peacekeeping because you spend points in ceroli and mysterious merchant on her. While you could spend them on rss and speedups. Decent for fighting barbs though.

- Pelagius: he is a decent commander for peacekeeping. Does his job but not as good as lohar and boudica.

- boudica: very good for peacekeeping. Gives good value just not as strong as lohar.

- Lohar: he is the best you could use for peacekeeping. Good for ap saving. Extremely good in early game.

C tier: 

- Eulji Mundeok: the casual epic commander that is not usable because of his lack health. He is not so strong out in the open field and he has barely any commander to pair with.  

- Wak Chanil Ajaw: is another casual epic commander that do great in the longevity, but barely does any good damage. This means he does last long but you would barely make a dent in the opponents march.  

- Kusonoki Masashige: is another casual commander leaning towards b tier though. He does a good job at garrison for your city and is decent with el cid and thutmose. But there is just better commanders for this job. 

B tier:

- Osman I: Osman is actually a decent second commander if you ever have a good 1st commander. The only problem with him is that there is a bit better commanders than him that could do better in that position.

- Catherine de’ Medici: gets unlocked in SoC only. Good value though.

- Narses: gets unlocked SoC only. Good value though.

A tier:

- Scipio Africanus: one of the best choices for power and strength on the field. Even though he was meta years ago, then still to this day he does work in some marches! He does good damage and is a straight up tank because of his damage reduction and healing factor!   

- Imhotep: is a strong commander when coming to debuffing and health gain! His skills combined make him a very strong partner with commanders like thutmose! Meanwhile his buffs like damage taken increase is very strong aswell!  

- Belisarius: he is the go to commander to pair as 1st commander with cao cao as second. Together they destroy the field with their march speed! Usually very good for the dirty trick of hitting farmers! Great way to annoy the enemy. Overall beli’s damage and march speed makes one of the best on the list.  

- - Björn Ironside: his strength out on the field always being the high damager. Even without any skill for health, then he does way better than almost all epic commanders. It is important to note that his 1st skill damage and second skill damage goes very good together! 

S tier: 

- Hermann: is the best choice for secondary archer and he could even go as 1st! His insane damage factor being the highest of all the epic archer commanders! His great skills all combined make him very strong with thutmose and el cid, he could even go as the 1st commander with them! His debuffs also do very good work by reducing the enemy rage bar by a 100 when the skill is maxed! Overall as a commander he does great damage and is very important for the archers in kvk 1.

S+ tier:

- Baibars: he is the best of the best when coming to his AoE! As a commander he thrives on the open field. He is fast, damaging and actually decently strong as a commander. his skills gives him a health factor of 200 while doing big direct damage, his fan is also the reason he is up on the S+ tier!   

- Sun Tzu: the best of the best epic commanders. Even years later, he is the meta for kvk 1 and also kvk 2 actually! His fan hitting strong with his damage that makes him a commander every other commander could pair with. He is strong because of his health boost while getting a nice skill damage bonus up to a whole 20%! 

Commander pairings tier list:

Top 7:

7. Björn Ironside + Sun Tzu: a strong pairing and lasts long. (not the biggest damager)

6. Thutmose + Imhotep: strong damager in ball fights and lasts decently (downside: a lot of cavs kvk 1 and the most expensive troop type.. 

5. Belisarius + Cao Cao: strong skill damager and very fast march speed! (not as useful in ball fights) 

4. Sun tzu + Æthelflæd: strong damager and god AoE (downside: not so long lasting)

3. Thutmose + Hermann: the best archer pairing with an epic. Does great value in damage and last pretty good. (downside: archers are pretty pricey to run)

2. Baibars + Sun Tzu: better than a lot of the pairings with gold commanders. Does incredible damage and has a surprising good strength (downside: inf counters it a bit, so watch out for those in the field)

Epic commander tier list
Made by benjamin.rok (Peanut)

Farmers:

  • Queen Tamar of Georgia: not usable for fights. Good for farming.

  • Joan of Arc: is usable for fighting because of her healing factor. But it is not as good as it was once.

Peacekeeping:
- Keira: not the best option for peacekeeping because you spend points in ceroli and mysterious merchant on her. While you could spend them on rss and speedups. Decent for fighting barbs though.
- Pelagius: he is a decent commander for peacekeeping. Does his job but not as good as lohar and boudica.

guides.title: Gang Gamchan Guide
guides.summary: Dominate 1v1 duels and shred single-target focus fire with relentless combo attacks! 🐎 The ultimate guide to the high-sustain Cavalry leader, Gang Gamchan.  Discover why Gang Gamchan is a niche skip for most open-field fighters, but an absolute monster when paired with combo-heavy commanders. This guide analyzes his dual combo strikes, massive healing scaling, and target-debuffing mechanics. Learn how to build his optimal Open Field talent tree, master top synergies with Achilles and King Arthur, and avoid open-field positioning errors that will cost you trades!
guides.content_markdown:
Gang Gamchan Guide

Made by: Peanut (benjamin.rok)

Should you invest in Gang Gamchan?

- For most players, the answer is no.

- 
Gang Gamchan is a powerful Cavalry commander built around combo attacks, survivability, and sustained single-target damage. While his damage output is excellent, he lacks any Area of Effect damage, making him less valuable in the large open field fights that dominate Rise of Kingdoms.

- 
If you already have Achilles or plan on using future combo-focused Cavalry commanders, Gang Gamchan becomes a much stronger investment. However, for most free-to-play players and low spenders, there are more versatile Cavalry commanders that provide greater value across multiple game modes.

What makes Gang Gamchan strong?

- Gang Gamchan is built around dealing massive combo damage while becoming increasingly difficult to kill.

- 
His active skill launches two powerful combo attacks while granting Cavalry Health and Defense, greatly increasing both his damage output and survivability. It also significantly boosts his healing for the next 5 seconds.

- 
His second skill reduces all incoming damage by 10% while providing 20% March Speed and 30% Cavalry Defense. These defensive bonuses allow him to stay in fights much longer than most Cavalry commanders.

- 
His third skill increases normal attack damage by 15% while converting a portion of combo attack damage into healing. This creates an incredible sustain engine during prolonged fights and allows him to continuously trade efficiently.

- 
His fourth skill gives combo attacks a chance to reduce the target's Defense by up to 40%, dramatically increasing both his own damage and the damage dealt by nearby allies focusing the same target.

Best Open Field Talent Tree:

![image1](replaceurl)

Best Pairings:

1. Achilles

Gang Gamchan's strongest pairing. Achilles provides excellent combo attack synergy and Area of Effect damage while Gang Gamchan adds survivability, healing, and powerful debuffs. Achilles should be the primary commander.

2. King Arthur

King Arthur is another excellent option that benefits greatly from Gang Gamchan's combo attack mechanics and defensive support. While not as strong as Achilles, they still create a durable and hard-hitting Cavalry march.

Tips and Tricks:

- Always use a full Cavalry march to activate all of his bonuses.

- 
Pair him with commanders that focus on combo attacks.

- 
Fight prolonged battles where his healing provides maximum value.

- 
Use him primarily in open field combat rather than rallies or garrisons.

- 
Expertise significantly improves both his sustain and survivability.

Biggest Mistakes:

- Do not invest in Gang Gamchan if you dislike single-target commanders. Most of his value comes from sustained damage rather than AoE.

- 
Do not expect him to perform like traditional AoE Cavalry commanders.

- 
Do not pair him with commanders that lack combo attack synergy.

- 
Do not overstay simply because of his healing. He is durable, but can still be focused down by multiple enemy marches.

guides.title: Gold Commander tier list (kvk 1)
guides.summary: Dominate the open field and crush your first KvK! ⚔️ The ultimate blueprint to navigating the early-game meta in Rise of Kingdoms. Discover exactly which legendary commanders are worth your precious resources—from S-Tier powerhouses like YSG to reliable tanks and high-damage cavalry leaders. Avoid sinking investments into useless, outdated traps and learn how to maximize your marches for long-term success right from the start!
guides.content_markdown:
Gold Commander tier list (kvk 1)

Made by: benjamin.rok (Peanut)

Tier list:

Overview of each commander:

S tier:

- YSG: is the best legendary commander when coming to kvk 1, his Rain of arrows does a huge damage factor up to 1400 when 5111 alone. He could do better than almost every commander in kvk 1 with his first skill, but the real deal is if you get him to 5515 where you get the destiny skill that unlocks up to 50% more skill damage which is an insane value. The last thing to talk about is when expertised then he has a circle AoE that is perfect in ball fights. Overall then he is very useful for barb chaining and even kvk 2 and SoC.

A tier:

- Charles Martel: now we go the the beef of tanking, charles martel that is sublime in the open field when it comes to defense, but also does a very good direct damage factor up to 1200. But the main thing about martel is his shield that absorbs damage for 4 whole seconds while getting attacked, with his health, defense and counterattack bonuses, then he does incredibly good when it comes to long lasting fights.  

- Thutmose: is a not as big damaging commander as the other 2 we have talked about, but the difference with thutmose is he actually acts as a very good tank on the field, he has bonuses like, attack, speed, damage, defense and then he takes away 30% of the healing of the attacking unit. Meanwhile he also does a skill damage increase up to 15% makes up for the 1000 skill factor. Overall he is the best pic for a main archer commander and has 4 skills that fit very well together.   

- Minamoto: is a very high A tier but not S. his damage factor is huge and does up to 1400, meanwhile he can even get an additional damage factor of 600. He also has his 4th skill that has a chance of him doing up to 30% more damage which makes him a very reliable commander that is not only fast on the map, but also very damaging.   

- Pyrrhus: is another highly damaging commander with up to 1400 damage factor, but the thing to take notice on is actually also the amount of different boosts he gives, he gives health, speed, normal damage and attack bonus which makes him a very tanky commander, meanwhile his 4th skill makes him take up to 20% less skill damage which is amazing for a tanky and highly damaging commander.  

- Mention: Pelagius Gold commander: is an A tier commander from the skill stats, i would possibly even call him a top A tier because of his skills. I do believe his damage factor with the rage gain is an incredible good 1st skill but also paired with his 4th skill of healing factor. I believe this could be a new meta in the early game.

B tier:

- æthelflæd: is one of the best valued commanders to use because she is free. You can grind expedition and unlock her that way. Her first skill does 800 damage factor meanwhile she has some nice boosts and debuffs like countterattack damage reduction and health, defense and attack reduction up to 30% making her a very good commander to pair with high damaging ones like sun tzu. Overall her ability to debuff and do a half circle AoE is very good.

- Mehmed: is actually a very strong commander for direct damage factor that goes up to 1150, he even deals up to 20% more skill damage which makes him a very strong second commander. The reason for him being in the b tier is because he is a leadership commander and also focuses a lot on the damage when he is rallying a city, 2 of his skills actually goes towards rally on cities which make those 2 skills useless in the field. 

- Richard: is a very strong commander on the field when it comes to being a tank, his healing factor going up to 1400 is a crazy good skill for him making him a strong tank commander, the reason he is in B tier is because Charles Martels overall performance on the field is a bit better making him the better pic. But if you are a high spender then richard can also be a go to commander choice for a tank.

- El Cid: is another great choice for an archer commander main, the only difference from him and thutmose is that el cid does single damage meanwhile thutmose does a fan shape. Otherwise el cid is a very decent pick to use against a single target. 

- Cao Cao: is a great commander when it comes to value, one of the new things making it so you can only unlock him the first 8 days of all gold commanders. This makes him valuable for barb hitting and also very liable as a secondary commander on the field, he does good single target damage and has a rage gainage of up to 100 while also having a healing factor.

C tier:

- Mulan: is a decent second commander, but there are much better commanders out there like mehmed, her reductions and buffs make her a decent choice but not as valuable.   

- Julius cæsar: is a not so valuable commander, he is a leadership commander that is mainly focused on hitting cities or garrisons, there are just way better options.   

- Ragnar Lodbrok: he is another leadership commander that only buffs his own march and the buffs are just not it on him, he is a decent commander but there is a reason he is down in c tier.  

- Frederick: once again a leadership commander that is too focused on rally, he has a 800 damage factor with a decent healing factor up to 1000, but the rest just makes him not good for the open field.  

- Siyaj K’ak’: a decent commander by his skills actually with 1000 damage factor, but just not the choice when you have thutmose and el cid way better than him overall.

D tier:

- Hannibal Barca: a very useless commander in my opinion, a leadership commander focused once again on rallying. Aswell as you need to spend a whole lot of money to just unlock him. It is 20$ to get 10 hannibal heads.

- Lu Bu: a commander you cannot get ingame anymore, so that is why he is ranked D tier, nothing much to add to that.

Gathering commanders:

- Cleopatra  

- Seondeok  

- Ishida Mitsunari

guides.title: Ivar Guide
guides.summary: Don't blow your hard-earned Legendary Sculptures on a highly specialized commander you might never use! 🪓 The ultimate tactical breakdown of the Infantry rally powerhouse, Ivar.  Discover why this commander is a top-tier asset for dedicated rally leaders but a complete trap for free-to-play and low spenders. This guide dissects his massive 2500 smite damage factor, explosive rage engine, and unique target-silencing mechanics. Master his optimal rally talent tree, uncover his best pairings like Scipio Aemilianus, and learn how to avoid the open-field mistakes that will crater your trading efficiency!
guides.content_markdown:
Ivar Guide

Made by: Peanut (benjamin.rok)

Should you invest in Ivar?

For most players, the answer is no.

- 
Ivar is one of the strongest Infantry rally commanders in Rise of Kingdoms, but almost all of his value comes from leading rallies against objectives. His kit is built around huge AoE damage, fast Rage generation, and powerful rally buffs, while offering very little in open field.

- 
If you are a rally leader with a maxed Infantry march, Ivar is an excellent investment. However, for free-to-play players, low spenders, and anyone who rarely leads rallies, he is an easy skip. There are commanders that provide value across multiple game modes, while Ivar is almost entirely locked to rallying.

What makes Ivar strong?

- 
Ivar is built around dealing massive burst damage during rallies.

- 
His active skill deals 2500 smite damage to up to 3 enemy targets, making it one of the hardest-hitting Infantry AoE skills in the game. It also grants 15 Rage per second for 3 seconds, allowing him to cycle skills extremely quickly.

- 
When used as the primary commander, his active skill also silences the target, creating a powerful burst window.

- 
His second skill grants:

30% Attack

10% Health

20% March Speed

- 
Unlike many rally commanders, these stats are always active and greatly strengthen Infantry marches.

- 
His third skill is where Ivar truly shines. While rallying cities or strongholds, he gains 20% extra smite damage, deals increased damage against Cavalry, and frequently gains additional Rage, allowing him to cast his active skill even more often.

- 
His fourth skill reduces incoming Combo Attack damage during rallies while also increasing your rally's damage whenever enemies trigger combo attacks.

Best Rally Talent Tree:

Best Pairings:

1. Scipio Aemilianus

Ivar's strongest pairing. Scipio applies a damage debuff before Ivar unleashes his 2500 damage factor active skill, creating one of the strongest Infantry rally combinations. Scipio should be the primary commander.

- Sun Tzu Prime

Sun Tzu Prime provides excellent Rage generation and sustained damage, allowing Ivar to cycle his active skill even faster.

Tips and Tricks:

- Only invest in Ivar if you regularly lead Infantry rallies.  

- Always use a full Infantry march.  

- Pair him with commanders that increase Rage generation and burst damage.  

- His silence only works when Ivar is the primary commander.  

- If you're free-to-play or a low spender, save your Legendary Sculptures for more versatile commanders.

Biggest Mistakes:

- Do not invest in Ivar just because of his high damage factor. Most of his value is locked behind rallying.  

- Do not use him in open field. Much of his kit becomes inactive outside rallies.  

- Do not prioritize him over versatile commanders unless you are a dedicated rally leader.  

- Do not expect a 5511 Ivar to compete with fully invested rally commanders. He benefits heavily from full expertise.

guides.title: Joan of Arc Guide
guides.summary: Unlock the ultimate support engine that remains relevant from early game all the way to late-game Canyon! 🌾 The definitive tactical guide to the premier epic buffer, Joan of Arc.  Discover why Joan of Arc breaks the traditional epic commander ceiling, delivering massive multi-march stat buffs and rapid rage generation to up to 5 surrounding marches. Learn how to leverage her versatile kit for Sunset Canyon, alliance support, and gathering, master her optimal talent builds, and pair her with commanders like Sun Tzu to maximize your team fight utility without spending a single Legendary Sculpture!
guides.content_markdown:
Joan of Arc Guide

Made by: Peanut (benjamin.rok)

Should you invest in Joan of Arc?

● maybe — one of the few epic commanders even advanced players keep using.

● Joan of Arc is a decent commander especially for canyon. 

● She provides extra rage and useful buffs to up to five marches at once, including allied marches, giving her rare large-scale utility.

● She remains relevant even for progressed accounts, which is unusual for an epic-tier commander.

What makes Joan of Arc strong?

● Her active skill grants extra rage to her troops, speeding up skill cycling for the whole march.

● Her buffs can extend to multiple marches simultaneously, including allies, making her valuable for group content.

● As an Integration commander with Gathering:Support specialty, she's also flexible enough to assist economically when needed.

Best Talent Trees:

- Gathering:

 

Best Pairings:

1. Sun Tzu

Combining two of the best epic commanders creates an incredibly strong, low-cost march for open field and canyon.

- Any legendary rally leader

Her rage buffs to multiple marches make her an excellent support pick alongside a strong rally leader.

Tips and Tricks:

guides.title: Liu Che Guide
guides.summary: Unleash a relentless barrage of smite damage and dominate the open field! ⚔️ The definitive guide to the Infantry powerhouse, Liu Che.  Discover why Liu Che is one of the safest, highest-value investments in Rise of Kingdoms, engineered to shred multiple enemy marches while remaining nearly unkillable in large ball fights. Learn why he shines best as a secondary commander, master his optimal Open Field talent tree, and explore top-tier pairings like Bai Qi and Sun Tzu Prime to maximize your trading efficiency!
guides.content_markdown:
Liu Che Guide

Made by: Peanut (benjamin.rok)

Should you invest in Liu Che?

- For almost every player, the answer is yes.

- 
Liu Che is one of the strongest Infantry commanders in Rise of Kingdoms and an excellent investment for both free-to-play players and spenders. His kit is built entirely around open field combat, offering exceptional smite damage, survivability, march speed, and consistent pressure during large fights.

- 
Unlike many Infantry commanders, Liu Che works extremely well as a secondary commander. His powerful skills provide almost everything he needs, while stronger Infantry talent trees from other commanders allow him to reach his full potential. If you're looking for a top-tier open field commander, Liu Che is one of the safest investments in the game.

What makes Liu Che strong?

- Liu Che is built around dealing massive smite damage while remaining difficult to kill.

- 
His active skill deals 2250 smite damage to up to 5 enemy targets while reducing their March Speed by 40% for 3 seconds. This creates huge value during large field fights by damaging multiple enemies while preventing them from escaping.

- 
His second skill grants 20% Infantry Defense, 20% March Speed, and 20% Skill Damage reduction when using a full Infantry march. These powerful stats greatly increase both his mobility and survivability.

- 
His third skill increases Infantry Attack by 20% and gives normal attacks a chance to deal additional smite damage, providing strong and consistent damage throughout every fight.

- 
His fourth skill increases normal attack damage by 10% and reduces the target's damage whenever Liu Che deals smite damage, making him both an offensive and defensive powerhouse in prolonged battles.

Best Open Field Talent Tree:

Best Pairings:

1. Bai Qi

Bai Qi is one of Liu Che's strongest pairings. He provides outstanding survivability, strong Infantry buffs, and excellent utility while Liu Che delivers massive smite damage. Bai Qi should be used as the primary commander.

- Sun Tzu Prime

Sun Tzu Prime offers exceptional Rage generation and sustained skill damage, allowing Liu Che to trigger his smite damage even more frequently. Together they create one of the strongest Infantry open field marches.

Tips and Tricks:

- Use Liu Che as a secondary commander whenever possible.

- 
Always run a full Infantry march to activate all of his bonuses.

- 
Pair him with commanders that provide strong Infantry talent trees.

- 
Focus on fighting in large open field battles where his AoE and smite damage shine.

- 
Expertise Liu Che to unlock his powerful extra normal attack mechanic.

Biggest Mistakes:

- Do not use mixed troop compositions, as you'll lose several of his strongest bonuses.

- 
Do not invest in Liu Che if your focus is rallying or garrisoning. He is designed almost entirely for open field combat.

- 
Do not use Liu Che as a primary commander unless necessary, as stronger Infantry talent trees provide better overall value.

- 
Do not underestimate his expertise. The additional normal attack significantly increases his sustained damage over longer fights.

guides.title: Matthias guide
guides.summary: Is the legendary defender Matthias a game-changing powerhouse or an expensive trap? 🏰 Discover the brutal truth about this specialized city garrison commander!  This guide breaks down why Matthias is an easy skip for 95% of players, despite his devastating 2400 damage factor AoE and relentless counter-activation skills. Learn the exact mechanics that make his city defense formidable, master his optimal talent tree, and check out his best pairings (like Lapulapu). Save your precious Legendary Sculptures, avoid costly investment blunders, and learn where your resources are actually better spent!
guides.content_markdown:
Matthias guide

Made by: Peanut (benjamin.rok) 

Should you invest in Matthias?

- 
For almost every player, the answer is no.

- 
Matthias is one of the strongest city garrison commanders in Rise of Kingdoms, but his value ends there. He is designed exclusively for defending your own city and offers almost nothing in open field, rallies, or objective garrisons. Unless you are a mega spender who enjoys taking rallies on your city, your Legendary Sculptures are far better invested elsewhere.

- 
For free-to-play, low spenders, and even most medium spenders, Matthias is an easy skip. There are commanders that provide value in multiple game modes, while Matthias is locked to one of the least common roles in the game.

What makes Matthias strong?

- Matthias is built entirely around making your city extremely difficult to rally.

- 
His active skill deals 2400 direct damage to up to 5 enemy marches, making it one of the strongest AoE skills available on a city garrison commander. Since rallies are almost always supported by multiple marches, this allows Matthias to constantly punish everyone standing around your city.

- 
On top of that, he provides excellent survivability. His second skill grants:

15% Attack

15% Defense

10% Health

- 
These are some of the highest permanent stat bonuses available on a commander and make every troop inside your city significantly stronger.

- 
His third skill adds another defensive layer by reducing incoming skill damage by 25% whenever your rage reaches 70%. At the same time, while defending your city, your troops gain an 800 damage factor shield every few seconds, making rallies much harder to break through.

- 
His fourth skill is where Matthias becomes especially annoying to fight. Every time your city is hit by a normal attack, there is a chance for him to immediately cast his active skill again. This means attackers can be punished by multiple 2400 damage factor AoE skills throughout the rally.

- 
When expertise is unlocked, your city gains another 10% damage bonus while also increasing the frequency of these additional active skill casts.

Best garrison talent tree:

Best Pairings

1. Lapulapu 

Lapulapu is Matthias' strongest pairing.

Both commanders revolve around dealing massive area damage while punishing enemy rallies. Together they constantly pressure every march surrounding your city while providing excellent survivability.

Lapulapu should be used as the primary commander to benefit from his stronger talent tree.

2. Wu Zetian

Wu Zetian remains one of the strongest defensive commanders in the game thanks to her incredible durability and defensive buffs.

She pairs very well with Matthias if you do not own Lapulapu.

3. Heraclius

Heraclius offers excellent defensive buffs together with additional utility against rallies.

A solid option for players who already invested into him.

4. Yi Sun-sin (YSS)

Although older than many modern commanders, YSS still provides decent mixed troop buffs and works well as a secondary option.

5. Amanitore

Amanitore remains another acceptable alternative if she is already available on your account.

Tips and Tricks:

- Only invest in Matthias if your account is specifically built around city defense.

- Never prioritize him over strong open-field commanders.

- Pair him with commanders that increase survivability and skill damage.

- Mixed troop city garrisons gain additional value from his second skill.

- Matthias performs best when enemy rallies are heavily swarmed since his AoE can constantly hit multiple marches.

- Always let another commander lead flags and passes; Matthias is designed for cities, not objectives.

- If you are free-to-play or a low spender, save your Legendary Sculptures for commanders that can be used in multiple game modes.

Biggest Mistakes:

- Do not invest in Matthias simply because his damage looks impressive. His value is almost entirely locked behind city defense.

- Do not use him in open field. Almost every modern commander will outperform him.

- Do not use him as a rally leader. His skills are not designed for offensive play.

- Do not prioritize him over versatile commanders. Open-field commanders will contribute far more to your account throughout every KvK.

- Do not think he replaces objective garrison commanders. Defending your city and defending flags or passes are completely different roles

guides.summary: Transform your Archer marches into high-survivability, high-damage death stacks! 🏹 The ultimate tactical breakdown for the open-field powerhouse, Qin Shi Huang.  Discover why Qin Shi Huang is a must-have investment for Archer mains, breaking the fragile "squishy Archer" stereotype with incredible defensive stats and unique Rage-conversion mechanics. Master his passive Eternal Emperor AoE mechanics, build his optimal Open Field talent tree, and explore dominant pairings with Zhuge Liang and Yi Seong-Gye to crush enemy murder balls and secure top-tier trades!
guides.content_markdown:
Qin Shi Huang Guide

Made by: Peanut (benjamin.rok)

Should you invest in Qin Shi Huang?

For almost every player, the answer is yes.

- 
Qin Shi Huang is one of the strongest Archer commanders in Rise of Kingdoms and an excellent investment for both free-to-play players and spenders. His kit is built entirely around open field combat, providing incredible Area of Effect damage, high survivability, and unique Rage-based mechanics that constantly pressure enemy marches.

- 
Unlike most Archer commanders, Qin Shi Huang isn't overly fragile. His skills grant significant Defense and Health, allowing him to survive much longer in large field fights while continuously dealing damage. If Archers are your primary troop type, Qin Shi Huang is one of the best commanders you can invest in.

What makes Qin Shi Huang strong?

- Qin Shi Huang is built around converting Rage into massive sustained AoE damage.

- 
His unique mechanic converts his normal attacks into direct damage by consuming Rage. Whenever this happens, nearby enemies are also hit through the Eternal Emperor effect, allowing him to constantly spread damage across multiple marches.

- 
His second skill grants Archer units 20% March Speed, 30% Defense, and an additional 20% Health when using a full Archer march. These powerful defensive stats solve one of the biggest weaknesses of Archer commanders.

- 
His third skill activates automatically after entering combat, dealing additional AoE damage while draining Rage from enemy troops. This greatly reduces enemy skill cycling while increasing his own battlefield impact.

- 
His fourth skill grants 500 Rage when entering combat as the primary commander while reducing both incoming normal damage and large bursts of skill damage, making him surprisingly durable during prolonged fights.

Best Open Field Talent Tree:

Best Pairings:

1. Zhuge Liang

Qin Shi Huang's strongest pairing. Zhuge Liang provides incredible Rage generation, massive skill damage, and additional AoE, creating one of the strongest Archer marches in the game. Zhuge Liang should be the primary commander.

- Yi Seong-Gye

Yi Seong-Gye is an excellent secondary option thanks to his devastating circular AoE damage and strong Rage generation. Together, they create constant pressure in large open field fights by dealing continuous damage to multiple enemy marches, making them a great choice for murder balls and field combat.

Tips and Tricks:

- Always use a full Archer march to activate all of his bonuses.

- 
Pair him with commanders that increase Rage generation and skill damage.

- 
Use him primarily in large open field fights where his AoE reaches maximum value.

- 
Qin Shi Huang performs best as a secondary commander behind a stronger Archer talent tree.

- 
Expertise greatly improves his sustained damage and overall battlefield impact.

Biggest Mistakes:

- Do not use mixed troop compositions, as you'll lose his strongest stat bonuses.

- 
Do not use Qin Shi Huang for rallies or garrisons. His kit is designed almost entirely for open field combat.

- 
Do not underestimate his survivability. His defensive skills make him much tankier than most Archer commanders.

- 
Do not skip his expertise if you plan to main Archers. It significantly improves his sustained AoE damage throughout every fight.

    Charles martel matches perfect for a tanky march with sun tzu, he is great in the field and lasts long for sun tzu to keep firing his skill as a secondary commander.

  3. Æthelflæd
    A great F2P choice with æthelflæd being a very good secondary commander with a great AoE. this march can be squishy though.

Tips and Tricks:
● Prioritize him early — he's one of the best value-for-investment commanders in the game.

● Use him as a secondary commander to boost a strong legendary's skill damage and rage generation. Except with other great secondary commanders like YSG.

● Take advantage of his defensive stats when garrisoning your city.

Biggest Mistakes:
● Do not overlook him just because he's an epic commander — he outperforms many legendaries in his role.

● Do not use him purely as a primary if you have better damage-focused legendaries available; he shines more as support.

● Do not skip his expertise — his 5th skill adds meaningfully to his overall value.

guides.title: Sun Tzu Prime Guide
guides.summary: Supercharge your Infantry marches with the ultimate fast-cycling nuker! ⚔️ The definitive strategy guide to the open-field meta-god, Sun Tzu Prime.  Discover why Sun Tzu Prime is an essential investment for nearly every player, powered by a game-changing 900 Rage active skill requirement that lets him unleash devastating 3000 smite damage faster than almost anyone on the map. Learn how his Military Sage effect spreads true damage across enemy lines, build his optimal Open Field talent tree, and master top-tier synergies with Bai Qi and Liu Che to dominate large open-field battles!
guides.content_markdown:
Sun Tzu Prime Guide

Made by: Peanut (benjamin.rok)

Should you invest in Sun Tzu Prime?

- For almost every player, the answer is yes.

- 
Sun Tzu Prime is one of the strongest Infantry commanders in Rise of Kingdoms and an outstanding investment for both free-to-play players and spenders. His incredibly fast Rage cycle, massive smite damage, and exceptional synergy with other Infantry commanders make him one of the best open field commanders in the current meta.

- 
What truly sets Sun Tzu Prime apart is his 900 Rage requirement instead of the standard 1000. This allows him to cast his active skill significantly more often, creating more damage, more Rage generation, and greater pressure throughout every fight. If Infantry is your main troop type, Sun Tzu Prime is a commander you should absolutely invest in.

What makes Sun Tzu Prime strong?

- Sun Tzu Prime is built around fast skill cycling and devastating smite damage.

His active skill requires only 900 Rage and deals 3000 smite damage to a single target. Through his Military Sage effect, every instance of smite damage also deals additional true damage to nearby enemies, allowing him to spread damage while ignoring Attack and Defense modifiers.

- 
His second skill grants Infantry 25% March Speed, 20% Health, and 30% Attack while fighting in the open field. These powerful stats make him both highly mobile and extremely difficult to defeat.

- 
His third skill provides 20% Infantry Defense, increases smite damage, and gives basic attacks a chance to trigger additional smite damage, dramatically increasing his sustained damage throughout long engagements.

- 
His fourth skill reduces incoming damage by 10% while generating additional Rage whenever Military Sage deals true damage. This creates a powerful feedback loop that allows Sun Tzu Prime to cycle his active skill even faster.

Best Open Field Talent Tree:

Best Pairings:

1. Bai Qi

Bai Qi is Sun Tzu Prime's strongest pairing. Bai Qi's powerful smite damage perfectly activates Military Sage, creating constant Area of Effect damage while greatly increasing Sun Tzu Prime's overall damage output. Bai Qi should be the primary commander.

- Liu Che

Liu Che is another exceptional pairing thanks to his massive smite damage and sustained pressure. Together they create one of the strongest Infantry marches for large open field battles.

Tips and Tricks:

- Expertise Sun Tzu Prime as soon as possible. His expertise greatly improves his Area of Effect damage.

- 
Always use a full Infantry march to activate all of his bonuses.

- 
Pair him with commanders that deal smite damage to maximize Military Sage.

- 
Use Rage-generating equipment like Horn of Fury to speed up his already fast skill cycle.

- 
Focus on large open field fights where his true damage can hit multiple enemy marches.

Biggest Mistakes:

- Do not stop at 5511. Sun Tzu Prime gains a massive increase in damage from his expertise.

- 
Do not pair him with commanders that lack smite damage synergy.

- 
Do not use mixed troop compositions, as you'll lose several of his strongest Infantry bonuses.

- 
Do not underestimate his fast Rage cycle. It is the core mechanic that makes him one of the strongest Infantry commanders in the game.

guides.title: The Cao Cao Guide
guides.summary: The essential guide to maximizing Cao Cao as a "Gold Key" commander. Learn why he is the best early-game pick for barbarian hunting, map mobility, and daily Action Point generation—and why you should never waste universal gold sculptures on him. Includes talent tree, skill breakdown, and commander swap strategies for KvK 2
guides.content_markdown:
Made by: benjamin.rok (peanut)

## Cao Cao (double C)

### Is Cao Cao worth it?

Cao Cao is one of the best commanders in the early game to use for hitting barbs or barb forts. 

Cao Cao is a gold key commander. That is the reason why you should not use gold sculptures on him. (you open gold keys your whole time while playing RoK, when you max him then his gold key sculptures are useless, meanwhile gold sculptures can always be used on something else)

March speed, he has the mobility talent tree to help him run fast. 

His new passive skill gives him a daily 50 extra action points. This can sound like it’s not a lot, but by stacking this up over days, then you can achieve big numbers of speedups and resources.

Overall then Cao Cao is one of the most valuable gold key commanders because of his attributes. He can run fast for hitting barbs, and forts. Meanwhile he can go after runes or even run the ark in your ark of osiris match. Meanwhile his passive skill gives a very good passive income of action points.

### Talent tree:

- 
Cavalry: the cavalry stat can give a huge boost on the damage cao cao gives. all cavalry commanders have this talent and it is a pretty basic talent that assures a stable cavalry commander.

- 
peacekeeping: the peacekeeping gives the ability for Cao Cao to be one of the best early game commanders to attack barbs and barb forts. Some of the most valuable talents there are trophy hunters that give extra resource packs from hitting barbs. Meanwhile, the mighty force gives an added percentage of attack towards barb forts. Peacekeeping is also a good talent for cao cao because of his mobility.

- 
mobility: the mobility gives cao cao the best buffs to be the fastest march on the field, that is why cao cao can save a lot of time by doing barbs, barb forts, collect runes and run the ark in ark of osiris. 

All these talents combined make Cao Cao one of the greatest gold key commanders in the game.

### Skills:

- Cao cao’s first skill dragon rider gives the direct damage factor going up to 1400 when getting it to level 5. It also gives an attack reduction to your opponent of 40% meanwhile a march speed reduction up to 10% on your opponent aswell. This skill is the pillar to him being still strong on the field. 

- Cao cao’s second skill The Qingzhou army gives cao cao access for a bigger damage percentage towards barbarians all the way up to 50%. Meanwhile his passive skill gives up to 100 action points which is the reason for him being an even more valuable commander today.

- Cao cao’s third skill tiger knight gives him a march speed bonus when using cavalry, it can be up to 10% meanwhile he also gets an attack bonus up to 30%. These bonuses are very useful when his march is full cavalry.

- Cao cao’s fourth skill lofty ambition gives him a healing factor up to 1000 which makes Cao Cao the commander he is, this skill makes him one of the best of the gold key commanders. Meanwhile he also gets a rage gain of up to 100 which makes him valuable to max but only with gold keys. 

### Gold key new structure:

- The new gold key system has done so for the first 8 days of the kingdom where you can only unlock Cao Cao. this means that gold key commanders like charles martel and so on, are not in the gold key rewards list. 

- this makes it way easier to unlock Cao Cao and even get his skill very high on the first 8 days. 

- the only disadvantage is that you are not able to unlock any other gold key commander, and then you would have to save your gold keys that could generate a very good amount of speedups and resources. 

### Commander swap:

When you have finished kvk 2, then something named commander swap comes into the game. This event makes you able to unlock new commanders, meanwhile you can also switch a commanders skill tree for another one.

This is why Cao Cao is one of the most worth it commanders to invest in, because he is good in kvk 1 and pretty decent in kvk 2.

When you finish kvk 2, then Cao Cao is pretty useless except doing barbs and using his relics, but meta commanders end up being some of the best for chaining and so on. That is why you would want to commander swap Cao Cao as he would be one of the commanders you have with the most skill.

When you commander swap, then you would need to choose the meta, that is why you should always be up to date about which commander is the current meta.

### Commander pairings:

- Minamoto primary x Cao Cao secondary: this is the strongest pairing Cao Cao could be in because of the great use of rage, healing and damage factor all packed together making them one of the strongest commander pairings for the early game.

- Baibars primary x Cao Cao secondary: this is one of the best F2P friendly commander pairings when aiming for a Cav march. Baibars is one of the most damaging purple commanders, which makes him the best choice to pair with Cao Cao.

- Pelagius primary x Cao Cao secondary: this commander pairing isn’t one of the best to use for field fighting, but it is a strong march to do barb fighting or barb fort hitting.

guides.title: Tokugawa Ieyasu Guide
guides.summary: Protect your hard-earned Legendary Sculptures from a niche investment trap! 🏯 The definitive strategic breakdown of the Infantry garrison commander, Tokugawa Ieyasu.  Discover why this defensive leader is a hard skip for most players due to his lack of essential anti-swarm mechanics. This guide analyzes his single-target 2400 smite damage, debuff-cleansing Tosho effect, and cascading shield triggers. Master his optimal garrison talent tree, explore his top pairings like Matthias, and learn how to avoid the open-field blunders that will decimate your trading efficiency!
guides.content_markdown:
Tokugawa Ieyasu Guide

Made by: Peanut (benjamin.rok)

Should you invest in Tokugawa Ieyasu?

- For almost every player, the answer is no.

- 
Tokugawa Ieyasu is a dedicated Infantry garrison commander in Rise of Kingdoms, but his value ends there. While he has solid shields, smite damage, and defensive buffs, his kit lacks the anti-swarm tools needed to compete with the strongest modern garrison commanders.

- 
For free-to-play, low spenders, and even most medium spenders, Tokugawa is an easy skip. Your Legendary Sculptures are far better invested into commanders that perform well in open field or can fill multiple roles. Unless you are building a dedicated garrison account, Tokugawa simply isn't worth prioritizing.

What makes Tokugawa strong?

- 
Tokugawa is built around increasing the survivability of Infantry garrisons through shields and sustained buffs.

- 
His active skill deals 2400 smite damage to a single target, reduces the enemy's Defense by 10%, and grants his troop a 600 damage factor Mighty Shield, providing both offense and survivability.

- 
His second skill gives Infantry a chance to gain 30% Attack for 4 seconds whenever they perform a normal attack or counterattack, allowing for strong sustained damage during long fights.

- 
His third skill increases all garrison damage by 10% while defending. Whenever the garrison deals smite damage, it can cleanse debuffs and build up to 20% Infantry Health through the Tosho effect, making the garrison increasingly difficult to take down.

- 
His fourth skill provides another layer of defense by granting a 1200 damage factor Mighty Shield whenever the garrison receives buffs, greatly improving survivability during prolonged rallies.

- 
When expertise is unlocked, Tokugawa gains additional AoE pressure by giving normal attacks and counterattacks a chance to deal smite damage to up to 3 enemy troops, with a much higher activation chance while shielded.

Best Garrison Talent Tree:

Best Pairings:

1. Matthias

Matthias is Tokugawa's strongest pairing. Together they provide excellent survivability, strong smite damage, and multiple shield effects that make rallies much harder to break.

- Lapulapu

Lapulapu adds significant AoE damage while complementing Tokugawa's defensive playstyle, making them a solid Infantry garrison combination.

Tips and Tricks: 

- Only invest in Tokugawa if your account is built for garrisoning objectives.  

- Always use a full Infantry garrison.  

- Pair him with commanders that provide shields and additional smite damage.  

- His Health stacks become stronger the longer the rally lasts.  

- If you're free-to-play or a low spender, save your Legendary Sculptures for commanders that can also perform in open field.

Biggest Mistakes:

- Do not invest in Tokugawa simply because of his strong shields. His value is almost entirely locked behind garrison defense.  

- Do not use him in open field. His garrison skills become inactive.  

- Do not prioritize him over versatile Infantry commanders that perform well across multiple game modes.  

- Do not expect him to replace the strongest meta garrison commanders, as his kit lacks the anti-swarm tools needed to consistently compete.

guides.summary: Master the game’s most versatile AOE nuker and transform your early-game account! 🎯 The definitive guide to the essential legendary commander, Yi Seong-Gye (YSG).  Discover why YSG is considered one of the highest-value investments in Rise of Kingdoms, powered by his game-changing 360-degree circular skill damage and a massive +50% skill damage boost. Learn why you must fully expertise him to unleash his true potential, master his optimal Open Field and Garrison talent trees, and explore top pairings like Hermann Prime and Zhuge Liang to dominate open-field battles and barbarian chaining!
guides.content_markdown:
Yi Seong-Gye Guide

Made by: Peanut (benjamin.rok)

Should you invest in Yi Seong-Gye?

- For almost every player, the answer is yes.

- 
Yi Seong-Gye is one of the most valuable legendary commanders in Rise of Kingdoms. His circular Area of Effect damage, incredible versatility, and ability to fit into multiple game modes make him a must-have commander for nearly every account. He performs exceptionally well in open field battles, barbarian chaining, rallies, and can even contribute to garrisoning.

- 
Although newer commanders eventually outperform him in the late game, Yi Seong-Gye remains one of the best investments for free-to-play players, low spenders, and even spenders during the early seasons. Few commanders provide as much long-term value.

What makes Yi Seong-Gye strong?

- Yi Seong-Gye is built around dealing massive Area of Effect damage.

- 
His active skill deals up to 1700 damage factor to 5 enemy targets in a circular area after expertise. Unlike cone-shaped skills, enemies surrounding your march are all hit, making him one of the strongest AoE commanders in the game.

- 
His second skill gives all troop types a 10% chance to restore 100 Rage while greatly increasing Archer Attack. The additional Rage allows Yi Seong-Gye to cast his active skill much more frequently.

- 
His fourth skill increases all active skill damage by 50%, dramatically boosting every skill cast and making him an incredible secondary commander for almost any skill damage pairing.

- 
His expertise upgrades his fan-shaped AoE into a circular Area of Effect, which is the biggest reason why expertising Yi Seong-Gye is so important.

Best Talent Trees:

- open field:

- Garrison:

Best Pairings:

1. Hermann Prime

Hermann Prime provides excellent Rage generation, Archer buffs, and strong debuffs while Yi Seong-Gye delivers devastating AoE damage. Hermann Prime should be the primary commander.

- Zhuge Liang

One of the strongest Archer pairings in the game. Both commanders deal enormous skill damage and can devastate multiple enemy marches during large field fights.

Tips and Tricks:

- Expertise Yi Seong-Gye as soon as possible. His expertise is where most of his value comes from.

- 
Use him as a secondary commander whenever possible to avoid being focused.

- 
Pair him with commanders that increase Rage generation or Skill Damage.

- 
Use him for barbarian chaining to greatly reduce Action Point costs.

- 
His versatility makes him one of the safest legendary investments in the game.

Biggest Mistakes:

- Do not stop at 5511. Yi Seong-Gye gains most of his strength from his expertise.

- 
Do not use him as a primary commander unless necessary, as experienced players will often target him first.

- 
Do not expect him to remain a top-tier commander forever. His strength gradually falls off as newer commanders are released.

- 
Do not skip investing in him if you're an early-game player. He provides value in more game modes than almost any other legendary commander.

guides.title: Alliance mobilization guide
guides.summary: Work together with your alliance to complete timed individual quests and climb the MOB tier ranking system! This guide details roster registration requirements, how to manage your 10-quest limit, and tips for alliance officers to refresh the active quest pool to maximize both personal and alliance points safely.
guides.content_markdown:
## Alliance mobilization Guide

## Registration Requirements

Only alliance leaders or designated officers are allowed to register the alliance for the event. Each alliance must register between 30 and 150 participants. Leadership can modify the registered roster at any point before the registration period closes.

To be eligible, a player must already be a member of the alliance before registration is submitted. A minimum City Hall level of 16 is required. Each player is only allowed to participate under a single alliance for the duration of the event.

## Event Mechanics

All alliances are placed into randomized matchups against other alliances. Progress is made by completing individual quests, which contribute points toward both personal and alliance totals.

A maximum of 40 quests can be active in the pool at any time. Each player is restricted to holding one quest at a time.

Quests operate on a timer and will disappear if not completed and properly claimed before expiration. If a quest is not finished, the attempt is consumed and is not returned.

Example: a quest requiring 11 million resources will fail if only 8 million is gathered, resulting in a lost attempt.

If a quest is accidentally accepted, it can be safely ignored by allowing it to expire without completion or claim. This will free up a new quest without using up an attempt.

## Quest Limits

Each player has a maximum of 10 completed quests for the event. An additional quest attempt can be purchased for 600 gems.

## Ranking and Progression

All alliances begin at the Bronze tier. Advancement to higher tiers depends on prior MOB ranking performance. As alliance members complete quests, the total alliance score increases, which raises the event level.

A minimum of one completed quest is required for a player to qualify for final rewards.

## Additional Rules

Players are locked to the alliance that registered them and cannot complete quests or claim rewards elsewhere.

Alliance officers have the ability to refresh available quests to generate new options, with a 5-minute cooldown between refresh actions. After a quest is completed or refreshed, a new one will appear after a 5-minute delay.

## Quest Point System

Legendary quests award 200, 220, or 240 points. Epic quests award 120, 150, 160, or 180 points. Elite quests award 50, 60, or 90 points.

guides.title: Ark of osiris guide
guides.summary: Master RoK’s premier biweekly PvP event to secure crucial progression rewards, including 10 Gold Heads. This guide details essential alliance preparation steps, map structure mechanics, and top battlefield strategies—like the "murder ball" tactic—to help you efficiently reach your 10,000 personal point milestone risk-free.
guides.content_markdown:
# Ark of Osiris (AoO) Guide

Ark of Osiris (AoO) is an important event for overall account progression. Developing a strong understanding of the event and its mechanics will improve your performance and increase your value as a contributor within your alliance.

# What is Ark of Osiris?

Ark of Osiris, commonly referred to as AoO, is a biweekly PvP event held during weekends. In this event, two alliances from different kingdoms compete against each other in a structured battlefield environment.

Depending on the league format, alliances register a specific number of participants:

- Silver League: 15 players  

- Gold League: 30 players

In addition, alliances may designate up to 10 substitute players.

# Objectives & Rewards

The primary individual objective is to reach 10,000 personal points during the match, which rewards players with 10 Gold Heads.

During the battle, both alliances compete to:

- Capture structures across the map  

- Defend controlled objectives  

- Fight opposing players  

- Accumulate points over the duration of the match

The alliance with the highest total score at the end of the event is declared the winner.

The map includes the following structures:

Outpost of Seth/Iset, Obelisk, Shrine of Life, Desert Altar, Shrine of War, Sky Altar, and the central objective, the Ark.

# Ark of Osiris (AoO) Preparation & Strategy

## How to Prepare

Before participating in Ark of Osiris, contact your alliance leadership (R4/R5) to confirm whether you are eligible to join the upcoming match. If approved, prepare your account by ensuring the following:

- All marches and troops are inside your city before matchmaking begins  

- War Frenzy is inactive  

- Attack and Defense boosts are activated  

- Troop expansions are not used  

- You are online and ready before the event starts

Once matchmaking opens, enter the event immediately. There will be a preparation phase before combat begins.

During this time:

- Follow all alliance markers placed by R4/R5  

- Read alliance instructions carefully  

- Position yourself according to the alliance strategy

Most alliances operate with a defined battle plan, and following leadership instructions is critical. If no specific strategy is provided:

- Stay grouped with allied players  

- Join rallies whenever possible  

- Move collectively when engaging enemy players

When the battle officially starts:

- Deploy your strongest march immediately  

- Use remaining marches to reinforce rallies and objectives

# How to Reach 10,000 Points

Points in Ark of Osiris are earned through:

- Defeating enemy troops  

- Capturing and holding structures  

- Gathering resources

It is possible to achieve 10,000 points without using healing speedups, although this becomes significantly easier as your account progresses over time.

# Strategy & Communication

Strategies vary from alliance to alliance. Always:

- Read alliance mails before the event  

- Ask R4/R5 for clarification if needed  

- Follow assigned tactics and positioning

Strong communication and coordinated movement are among the most important factors for success in Ark of Osiris.

# Frequently Asked Questions

## What is the best way to win?

Maintaining tight coordination with your alliance is the most effective strategy.

A commonly used tactic is the “murder ball,” where alliance members remain grouped together in a concentrated formation. This approach:

- Makes it more difficult for enemies to isolate individual marches  

- Allows your alliance to overwhelm opponents through concentrated pressure  

- Improves reinforcement and survivability during engagements

## Do I lose resources or speedups?

- You do not lose resources when healing troops in Ark of Osiris.  

- However, healing speedups may still be used if you choose to accelerate recovery times.

## Do I lose troops permanently?

No. Troops are never permanently lost in Ark of Osiris.

Even if your hospital capacity is exceeded during the match, all troops are automatically returned after the event concludes.

## What is the most efficient way to reach 10,000 points?

The fastest and most reliable methods are:

- Fighting enemy players  

- Joining rallies  

- Defending structures

These activities provide significantly more points than farming alone.

While gathering resources can contribute additional points, it is generally less efficient for reaching the 10,000-point milestone quickly.

Monitor your score regularly throughout the match and continue participating in combat until the objective has been reached.

 

Follow these guidelines to perform well in Ark of Osiris and secure your 10,000 points for the 10 Gold Heads.

guides.title: Ceroli crisis guide
guides.summary: Conquer this high-value, recurring 5-player cooperative event to earn Ceroli coins for top-tier shop rewards like materials and speedups. This guide covers crucial role selection tactics (Tank, AoE, or Support), proper engagement timing, and essential mechanics management to defeat all five bosses risk-free.
guides.content_markdown:
# Ceroli Crisis Guide

Ceroli Crisis is an excellent recurring event that provides valuable free rewards, making it particularly beneficial for F2P and low-spending players.

## What is Ceroli Crisis?

Ceroli Crisis is an event that generally appears every three weeks. During the event, players battle five different bosses, each rewarding Ceroli coins upon completion. These coins can then be exchanged in the Ceroli shop for various items.

### Recommended Shop Priorities

- Materials (highest priority purchase)  

- Teleports  

- Speedups

Players are matched into groups of five, creating a cooperative team environment. Before entering battle, each player selects one of three available roles:

- Tank  

- AoE (Area of Effect Damage)  

- Support

Each role provides access to three unique abilities that can significantly impact the outcome of the fight.

# Boss Strategy & Completion Tips

## Role Selection

- If you are not the highest-power player in your group, it is generally recommended to select the Support role.  

- Support allows you to:  

- Heal allied troops  

- Improve team survivability  

- Contribute consistently throughout the encounter

## Engaging the Boss

- Do not initiate combat unless:  

- You are assigned the Tank role  

- You are the strongest player in the group  

- Bosses heavily prioritize the first player who attacks them, making proper engagement timing extremely important.  

- Once the designated player begins the fight, all other players should immediately follow up to maximize damage output and distribute incoming damage efficiently.

## Team Coordination

- Always attack as a coordinated group.  

- Proper synchronization:  

- Reduces total damage taken by the team  

- Maximizes overall damage dealt  

- Increases the likelihood of completing encounters successfully

## Boss Mechanics

Every boss features unique mechanics that must be understood and respected during combat. Examples include:

- Area-of-effect attacks, such as arrow rain patterns with limited safe zones  

- Summoned enemy units that must be defeated before the boss can be damaged effectively  

- Pay close attention to boss abilities and battlefield indicators throughout the encounter.  

- Simply auto-attacking without reacting to mechanics will often result in your troops being eliminated during the fight, significantly reducing your team’s effectiveness.

# Additional Notes

- Ceroli Crisis is completely free to participate in.  

- Players do not lose:  

- Troops  

- Resources  

- Speedups  

- This makes it a highly efficient and low-risk event for obtaining valuable rewards and progression materials.

guides.title: Champions of olympia Guide
guides.summary: Dominate RoK's competitive, team-based objective mode! Learn how to coordinate flag control, build a balanced three-march setup, and secure game-changing central objectives like the Ark and boss buffs to climb the ranking system risk-free.
guides.content_markdown:
# Champion of Olympia (CoO) Guide

Champion of Olympia is a weekly event available from Friday through Sunday and features gameplay inspired by team-based objective games similar to League of Legends.

## What is Champion of Olympia?

Champion of Olympia is a competitive team event centered around capturing and controlling flags across the map. Each player controls three marches and can select commanders based on the age and progression of their account.

After completing several matches, players receive a rank. Progression is achieved through victories and consistent performance, allowing players to climb the ranking system over time.

### Rewards

- Weekly participation rewards, including Gold Heads for completing enough matches  

- Additional rewards based on final rank placement

The primary objective is to accumulate points by controlling flags throughout the match. The team with the highest score at the end of the game is declared the winner.

# How to Succeed in Champion of Olympia

Success in Champion of Olympia is highly dependent on coordination and teamwork. Whenever possible, it is recommended to queue with players from your kingdom, although participation with random teammates is still viable.

## Recommended March Composition

A balanced setup is strongly recommended:

- One tank-focused march  

- One high-damage march  

- One support-oriented march

## Gameplay Priorities

- At the beginning of the match, prioritize capturing flags rather than engaging in unnecessary fights.  

- Focus on coordinated team play and maintaining control of flags for extended periods.  

- Constantly monitor the center area of the map, as it often contains key objectives such as:  

- An Ark that can be delivered to a flag for points  

- A boss that grants powerful buffs  

- A high-value flag worth additional points  

- Each map contains different layouts and objectives, making adaptability an important factor in overall performance.  

- Remain active throughout the match by continuously rotating between objectives, capturing flags, and defending controlled areas.  

- Avoid remaining idle or disengaging from gameplay, as map presence and objective control are critical to victory.

# Additional Notes

- While the rewards may not be as valuable as those from some other events, Champion of Olympia is completely free to participate in.  

- Players do not risk losing resources or troops, making it a low-risk event with worthwhile rewards for active participation.

guides.title: Dark fortress guide
guides.summary: Rally together with your alliance to summon and destroy up to three powerful Dark Fortresses! This guide covers maximizing your Raid Coins during the preparation phase, coordinating up to eight simultaneous rallies per fortress, and driving up damage to boost alliance rewards by up to 10 times via the MVP system.
guides.content_markdown:
# Dark Fortress Raid Event Guide

## How the Event Works

## Stage 1: Raid Coin Collection

Alliance members earn Raid Coins by defeating barbarians on the map. These coins can then be donated through the event interface to increase the alliance’s total damage against Dark Fortresses.

This stage focuses on preparation and strengthening the alliance before the raid begins.

## Stage 2: Raid Setup

Once enough Raid Coins are collected, the alliance leader or a titled officer selects the raid time and location.

Up to 3 Dark Fortresses can be summoned for the alliance to attack. After summoning, the raid phase officially begins.

## Stage 3: Fortress Assault

During the raid, members form rallies to attack the summoned Dark Fortresses. Coordinated rally participation is required to deal maximum damage and perform efficiently in the event.

## Rewards System

Rewards are split into personal and alliance-based rewards.

Personal rewards are determined by the amount of damage you individually deal during the raid. Alliance rewards are based on the total combined damage dealt by all members.

The highest damage contributor becomes the MVP. Depending on the MVP’s total damage output, alliance rewards can be increased by up to 10 times.

## Important Rules

Each alliance can only initiate one raid per event, but multiple attacks can be launched against the same Dark Fortress during that raid.

Once the raid time is set, summoned Dark Fortresses appear either in the kingdom or Lost Kingdom and cannot be moved afterward. All fortresses must be summoned to the same map location.

Each Dark Fortress can be attacked by up to 8 rally armies simultaneously.

Players only receive rewards once per event. Dealing zero damage means no personal or alliance rewards are granted. However, players can still participate in another alliance’s raid to earn rewards.

Raid timing cannot be changed within 5 minutes of the scheduled start. Raids cannot be started during the final 60 minutes of the event.

Unused Raid Coins are converted into personal points when the event ends.

Players can only attack Dark Fortresses summoned by their own alliance.

guides.title: ESMERALDA'S HOUSE & DIG EVENT
guides.summary: Maximize your drop rates, avoid costly gem traps, and hit key milestone chests efficiently! 🔮 The ultimate Esmeralda's House & Dig Event Blueprint for Rise of Kingdoms. This guide breaks down the math behind pull rates, dynamic drop tables, and milestone rewards. Learn how F2P and budget players can leverage daily free and half-price spins, why high spenders should calculate exact gem budgets before chasing 5% Stat Legendary City Skins, and how Esmeralda compares mathematically to the VIP Shop and Wheel of Fortune. Discover how to hit value thresholds like 10 and 40 spins, stack spending across overlapping recharge events, and avoid partial pulls that leave your gems wasted!
guides.author: benjamin.rok
guides.content_markdown:
ESMERALDA'S HOUSE & DIG EVENT BLUEPRINT

CORE MECHANICS & STARTER SETUP

- Esmeralda Event Variance: Esmeralda's House (and themed variants like Dig / Prayer events) is a luck-based gem sink designed around spinning wheels, digging tiles, or pulling wishing coins for materials and cosmetics.

- City Skin Unlock Costs: Pulling specifically for the 5% Stat Legendary City Skin reward typically requires going all the way to maximum milestone completions, costing anywhere from 70,000 to 100,000+ gems depending on pull luck.

- Dynamic Drop Pools: Standard pull tables dilute high-value drops with low-tier equipment blueprints, resource packs, and 60-minute speedups, shifting the real event value into milestone chests rather than raw pulls.

STRATEGIC PLANNING & ROUTINE

- F2P/Low-Spender Daily Budgeting: Free-to-play and low-spending players should strictly stick to taking the daily free pulls and discounted half-price pulls (400 gems), stopping completely unless aiming for a specific threshold.

- Milestone Commitments: Never stop pulling midway through an un-milestoned tier; if committing gems, always hit fixed thresholds (such as 10, 40, 70, or 100 spins) to capture guaranteed bonus reward chests.

- Skin Valuation Assessment: Evaluate city skins on functional stats rather than aesthetics—only commit 80k+ gems if the skin grants a +5% health/defense buff for your absolute main KvK march.

- Materials vs. VIP Shop Comparison: At 100 spins, Esmeralda averages roughly 710–720 gems per Epic Material equivalent. Since VIP Shop weekly materials cost 600 gems, VIP Shop is mathematically superior for pure material progression.

- Gems per Gold Sculpture Math: Purely pulling for Universal Legendary Sculptures in Esmeralda yields significantly lower head-per-gem rates compared to "More Than Gems" or targeted "Wheel of Fortune" runs.

- Inventory Chest Retention: Save blueprint choice chests and specialized equipment materials gained from milestone claims in your inventory until completing an entire gear piece build.

TIPS & TRICKS FOR FAST GROWTH

- The 10-Spin & 40-Spin Thresholds: For mid-spend players, stopping at the 10-spin or 40-spin milestone provides the best "value-per-gem spent" ratio for extra speedups and material chests.

- Pre-Event Gem Savings: If a meta-defining city skin appears in the event preview, hoard at least 90,000 liquid gems beforehand to guarantee reaching the skin milestone without buying expensive raw gem packs.

- Event Synergy Stacking: Time your heavy Esmeralda pulls during overlapping recharge or spending events to earn extra bonus rewards on top of Esmeralda's milestone chests.

CRITICAL MISTAKES TO AVOID

- Pulling for Skins Without a Full Budget: Never start pulling for a skin with only 30,000 to 40,000 gems in hand; failing to hit the final skin milestone leaves you with wasted gems and no skin.

- Ignoring VIP Shop Priority: Avoid dumping gems into Esmeralda if you have not yet reached VIP 14, as the daily 3 Universal Legendary Sculptures from VIP 14 offer far higher long-term account value.

- Over-valuing Secondary Drops: Do not justify going deep into the event for green/blue equipment blueprints or basic resource tokens—treat everything outside of epic/legendary materials, gold heads, and skins as filler.
